The separation the blocker was really about also holds: OBL-FX-AUTHORING's namedClassesNotAuthored lists exactly fourteen ids with no R-10 or R-6, both R obligations stand separately at leftoverDesign true, and G09 v3's own note — 'OBL-FX-AUTHORING remains the D-163 fourteen… R-10 and R-6 authoring is leftover on DR-105 beyond that fourteen' — is quoted verbatim in both their reasons. Zero wallClock, seconds, quoted millisecond unit, Date.now or timestamp anywhere in the file, and every bare integer is 2, 3, 5, 7, 08, 14 or 26 — versions, D-056 clause 5, file 08, the fourteen classes and required-now. Not one is an age, a bound or a duration. Of fourteen string fields touching envelope, journal, expiry, cleanup or wall-clock, thirteen are refusals or open-standing statements and the fourteenth quotes D-032's existing grant-journal blocker while keeping it STILL-ROUTED. The corpus the join relies on corroborates: permission-r6-r10-input-corpus.v2 carries journalBytes, expiryAge and cleanupBound as NOT-AUTHORED. Size was the other risk. Twenty-one obligations reconcile against twenty-one summary entries across six buckets with no gap, no duplicate and no flag-versus-bucket inconsistency.
